# Diagnostic sampling qualification

Issue #454 extends the existing gridded field service to MATLAB-supported profiles and fixed, moving and event positions. Spatial diagnostics are evaluated on their natural grid before interpolation. Initial/actual density selection, periodic horizontal and bounded vertical interpolation, active outputs, event ownership, transactional publication and bounded temporary storage remain explicit. Scalar, coefficient and vertical-profile-only restrictions are retained. MATLAB production changes are confined to the independent SQG tracer fix in PR #468.

The generated standard assembly has 1,754 rows: 1,732 supported fixture assignments, 22 intentional MATLAB incompatibilities and zero unqualified rows. Its 820 spatial rows reference the independent sampling fixture; 48 density sampling rows additionally reference the actual/initial fixture. Removing 40 redundant constant-adapter moving rows changes the row count from 1,794 while completing all 566 original #454 gaps. Fixture assignment is distinct from the final standard-parity decision in #307.

The final receipts bind tested source files and binaries. The C++ binaries were built from `a74ed4e61bc1bc57f731c999d7d404f8732f8679` plus the recorded source closure, subsequently committed as `ec280251`; the integration branch also contains independently qualified #467 through `19041fd2`. That merge changes `WVModel.addTracer`, which neither sampling fixture invokes. Scientific tests, interpolation formulas and tolerances were not changed during final qualification.

## Verification ledger

- Seven focused C++ programs pass in native Release and AddressSanitizer builds. They cover constant derived moving fields, density and forcing sampling, explicit rejections, owner and geometry lifetimes, inactive output, alias rejection, staged sibling failure, shared density recovery and temporary-memory bounds.
- The comprehensive MATLAB sampling fixture covers all six families, AA0/AA1, reference/native providers, linear/spline interpolation, wrapped horizontal coordinates, vertical endpoints/out-of-domain positions and varied full-column profiles. It records 7,136 independent comparisons plus 576 actual/initial density-reference comparisons. A second comparison against interpolation of the C++ completed grid separates interpolation errors from independently qualified density recovery tolerances.
- Three output methods cover representative constant nonhydrostatic and Hydrostatic ordinary/dense particle and mooring outputs, fixed/adaptive integration, both density references, two destinations and MATLAB/C++ continuation in both directions. Matched controls require exactly unchanged coefficients, particle positions and step/rejected/RHS counts, with zero density work when no density diagnostic is requested.
- Six variable-catalog tests pass. All seven matrix tests pass across the coherent batch and the targeted regenerated-file rerun. The initial stale-output-root failure remains in the development archive. The cheap provenance gate checks 1,754 rows and 75 witnesses.
- Code Analyzer reports zero findings in both changed sampling test classes, the compatibility test and variable generator. The assembly definition has five informational dynamic-string-array growth messages; the compatibility document generator has one obsolete-suppression message. These do not affect runtime scientific work.
- `docs:check` validates 2,026 files and 4,145 routes with zero failures or documentation drift. The 51 CI-policy tests and repository/source-artifact checks pass, including after merging the independent tracer change.

`development-receipts.json.gz` preserves earlier failed and provisional passes with their original labels. Failures include a protected MATLAB test-helper call, the independently filed ClassAnnotations #2 removal defect, a barotropic test geometry assumption, old event ownership behavior, and the particle diagnostic admission defect fixed here. No failed result is counted as final qualification.

The annotation-removal bug is tracked separately at https://github.com/JeffreyEarly/class-annotations/issues/2. The test fixture uses the existing operation-replacement API. No released package snapshot or ClassAnnotations source is changed by this work.

## Matched unrequested-path performance protocol

The prepared driver compares the frozen optimized-main runner (`b71860fc`, whose compiled source closure is identical to `a74ed4e6`) with the final #454 runner. It reuses the immutable #455 constant-nonhydrostatic and Hydrostatic 256×256×129 composite fixtures: coefficient and ordinary/dense velocity output, moving particles and full-volume tracer advection, with no newly requested diagnostics. It does not repeat kernel algorithm selection or measure small-grid speed.

Each profile has two excluded warmup pairs and eight alternating measured pairs. Every candidate/control NetCDF graph must match exactly; the first measured pair also checks the existing MATLAB oracle using its original tolerance. Each profile must satisfy the 1.03 integration-time ratio; the equal-profile paired bootstrap upper 95% bound must also be at most 1.03. Full-model retained growth is bounded by the derived 368 bytes of fixed metadata: five event-plan slots ×64, one moving-plan member ×16 and two prepared geometries ×16. No new retained scientific volume is permitted. Complete-process timings and RSS are recorded separately.

The driver verifies fixture, request, source, executable and helper hashes before/after measurement, retains both first measured outputs and all failures, and deletes only successfully compared later payloads. To reproduce in the recorded local environment, copy `unrequested-performance-driver.py` to a new temporary directory and run it with `/private/tmp/wvm455-model-venv/bin/python`, passing candidate SHA `c8e87d1c51a3f30e634fd33c24a7df2ff612973f52419d9a24908c86a6bc12bd`. The script creates its `campaign` sibling and refuses to overwrite it.

These committed receipts establish numerical qualification and freeze the measurement protocol. See [issue #454](https://github.com/JeffreyEarly/wave-vortex-model/issues/454) for the subsequent performance receipt and merge decision. Performance qualification was awaiting an idle host when this receipt was committed; the unrelated JPO2026 experiment was left running.
